$what: Provenance of aurora-regions.schema.json, empyrean's CONTRACT schema for an act's regions document, vendored into Aurora beside the codec that validates against it. document.ts imports the .json directly; this sidecar records where those bytes came from, and test/formats/regions-schema-drift.test.ts reads `empyrean.blob` from here as its pin of record.
$why_a_sidecar_and_not_only_a_test_const: Because nothing hashes a comment. The scene schema's pin lived as a `const` in its drift test and as prose in two more files, and the prose copy went THREE re-pins stale without anything going red. The hash lives HERE, once, machine readable, and the test reads it. Every prose citation of a hash in this repo, including the ones in this file's own pin history, is prose and says so.
$why_vendored: Aurora's core must validate from a lone clone, inside a git worktree (where ../../empyrean is not where it is from master), and in a packaged Electron build that ships no sibling repo. A path probe design would degrade to 'schema not found, so skip validation', which is the loud-on-unmeasurable failure this suite is not allowed to have. The cost of vendoring is staleness; the drift gate and the currency check are the payment. This file is never read from a sibling checkout at runtime or at test time by path, only through git objects at a named revision (docs/reviews/2026-08-28-golden-live-tree.md is the defect that made reading a peer's LIVE WORKING TREE unacceptable).
$why_not_under_test_fixtures: This is a SOURCE file the app imports, not a test fixture, so it lives beside its consumer. The same reason the scene and preset schemas do: the published-revision sweep in test/formats/aeon-fixture-currency.test.ts walks test/fixtures/ and reads a `revision` key inside a block it knows; a schema the RENDERER needs at runtime cannot live under test/ at all, whatever the sweep does.

what_this_pin_carries: THE FIRST RE-PIN OF THIS FILE, so unlike the entry it replaces there IS a diff to read, and it is TWO LINES at /$defs/bg/properties/layoutRef and nothing else: the pattern widened from ^(@act|[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,31})$ to ^(@act|[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{0,127})$, and the description gained the reason. WHY empyrean widened it: `bg.layoutRef` CITES aurora's background library instead of minting an id, and the library's real ids are hyphenated and timestamped (deep-forest-v15-marching-colonnade-1781232423352), so the old minted-id pattern matched 0 of 17 real entries and no background was spellable in a schema-legal document. It is modelled on `preset` on the same object, which cites the game's effects library the same way. NOTHING IN AURORA OWES A DATA MIGRATION, and that is a measurement rather than a hope: the amendment only ACCEPTS MORE, every `bg` in the shared golden is null today, and every layoutRef value this repo's sources, tests and vendored vectors carry (`@act`, `ojz_forest`, `forest_bg`, `no_bg`, `nope`) is legal under BOTH the old pattern and the new — so no assertion in this repo had to be widened to keep the suite green, which is the move a re-vendor must never make. NO KEYWORD WAS ADDED: the keyword-coverage and per-node rows of regions-schema-drift.test.ts needed no json-schema-subset.ts edit, MEASURED by running them over the new bytes and not assumed from the size of the diff. THE FOUR OTHER PATTERNS IN THIS FILE ARE UNTOUCHED and still carry {0,31} — the region `id`, `preset`, `rasterRef` and `sceneRef` are MINTED here rather than cited from a foreign namespace, which is the distinction the amendment turns on, so a grep that finds {0,31} still in this file has not found a missed re-vendor.
the_hole_this_pin_carries: `bg.span` is DERIVED FROM THE REFERENCED LAYOUT AND NEVER TYPED BY HAND (part 2 section 6.2 item 1), and NO KEYWORD IN THIS FILE CAN SAY SO. The schema asserts only 'integer, at least 1'; Aurora's codec has no background layout library yet, so a hand-edited span that disagrees with the layout `bg.layoutRef` names is accepted here, round-tripped unchanged, and left for the generator to catch. Recorded as a hole rather than left as a silence, because a schema that validates the key reads as a schema that checks it. The schema's own description lists four more of the same kind: that `preset` names a record that exists, that `layoutRef` names a layout in the library, that a rectangle lies inside the act, and that the union of referenced layouts fits BG_TILE_CAPACITY. THIS RE-PIN WIDENS THAT HOLE ON PURPOSE AND SAYS SO: the amendment's own description ends "let the GENERATOR validate that the id resolves. Existence is not this schema's job", so the schema now accepts 128 characters of hyphenated spelling and checks none of it. Aurora is not silent on that half — `src/core/formats/regions/validate.ts` carries §2.5 rule 6, which resolves `bg.layoutRef` against the background library it has loaded and reports an unresolved or bodyless layout as a load-time notice — but that is a NOTICE in this repo and not a refusal, and it is not in the contract.
